case-1.objects: A finite site set I = Fin(n + 1), a family of coordinate spaces X(j), their dependent product Ω = ∏_{j∈I} X(j), a measure μ on Ω, a selected site i ∈ I, a configuration x ∈ Ω, and the actual heat-bath kernel heatBath X μ i. The retained-coordinate map r_i sends y to (y(i.succAbove j))_{j∈Fin(n)}, and F_i(x) = {y ∈ Ω : r_i(y) = r_i(x)} is its fiber at x.
case-1.domains: n ∈ ℕ; j ranges over Fin(n + 1) for the coordinate family and over Fin(n) for the retained tuple. The map i.succAbove identifies Fin(n) with the sites other than i. The domain and output state space of the kernel are Ω with its dependent-product measurable structure; the retained-tuple space is ∏_{j∈Fin(n)} X(i.succAbove j). The kernel evaluated at x and cond μ F_i(x) are both measures on Ω.
case-1.quantifiers: For every implicit n ∈ ℕ, every such family X with measurable structures, every finite measure μ on Ω, every site i with the indicated typeclass instances, and every configuration x ∈ Ω, if μ(F_i(x)) ≠ 0, then the stated equality holds. In the eventwise formulation the identity holds for every measurable S ⊆ Ω, at each x satisfying that premise, not merely almost everywhere.
case-1.assumptions: Each X(j) has a MeasurableSpace instance. μ has IsFiniteMeasure, i.e. μ(Ω) < ∞, not necessarily μ(Ω) = 1. The selected X(i) is StandardBorelSpace and Nonempty. The retained-tuple space has MeasurableSingletonClass, so the fiber is measurable as the preimage of the singleton {r_i(x)} under the measurable retained-coordinate map. The explicit premise hx is μ(F_i(x)) ≠ 0, hence 0 < μ(F_i(x)) < ∞.
case-1.conclusion: At the given x, heatBath X μ i x = cond μ F_i(x) as measures on Ω. Equivalently, for every measurable S ⊆ Ω, the transition measure assigns S the mass μ(F_i(x) ∩ S) / μ(F_i(x)). In particular the transition measure assigns mass one to the entire fiber.
case-1.senses: The fiber fixes all coordinates other than i and does not fix the selected coordinate. The nonzero premise is about the entire retained fiber, not the singleton {x}. HeatBath is the particular kernel built via measurable regrouping, pushforward, a one-block conditional update preserving the retained tuple, and transport back, not an unspecified version. The equality is pointwise under the positive-fiber premise and is an equality of full-state measures, not just a selected-coordinate marginal. It gives no claim here about null fibers, the mass of {x}, or μ being a probability measure.
case-1.constants: There are n + 1 sites and n retained sites, with no restriction excluding n = 0. The explicit mass threshold is 0 and the hypothesis is strict positivity, with no uniform positive lower bound. The normalization divisor is the actual fiber mass μ(F_i(x)), not the total mass or a fixed numerical constant; mass one is a consequence of the conditional normalization.
